title: Manifold Absolute Pressure and Temperature (MAPT) Sensor Removal and Installation
introduction: MAPT means manifold absolute pressure and temperature—think of it as the intake manifold's compact weather station. This procedure applies to the 2.3L EcoBoost (231kW/314PS). I use the illustrations as a layered map: remove the engine appearance cover, disconnect the sensor, then release its mounting retainer. The work here covers removal and refitting; diagnosing a pressure or temperature complaint requires a separate diagnostic test.

items.name: Confirm applicability
items.detail: Use this procedure for the specified EcoBoost engine. Have a torque wrench suitable for the small fastener torques given in the steps.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started during work, causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury. If equipped with engine auto start-stop, keep the ignition off when servicing near rotating engine parts, because the engine may otherwise start automatically and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Cooling-fan condition
items.detail: With the ignition OFF, inspect all cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation before underhood work. Do not work under the hood with a damaged fan; it must be replaced with a new fan before proceeding. A damaged fan can separate during operation and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Cooling-fan operation
items.detail: Cooling fans may run with the ignition off. Disable them before working nearby; unexpected operation may cause personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use the applicable protection may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before refitting the sensor; installation details are included alongside removal.
edits.why: The fastener torques are printed beside the removal operations and apply when those parts are secured during installation.

edits.text: Remove the nuts securing the engine appearance cover, then remove the cover. During installation, tighten the nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).
edits.why: Removing the cover exposes the sensor work area. I use the highlighted mounting nuts in the first drawing to distinguish the cover hardware from the sensor retainer underneath.

edits.text: Disconnect the MAPT sensor electrical connector at the connection highlighted in the sensor illustration.
edits.why: Disconnecting the wiring first frees the sensor electrically before its mounting retainer is removed.

edits.text: Remove the MAPT sensor retainer, then remove the sensor from the manifold. During installation, tighten the retainer to 44 lb.in (5 Nm).
edits.why: The sensor drawing separates the electrical connection from the mechanical mounting point. Its tightening value belongs to the sensor retainer, whose specification differs from the cover hardware.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: install the MAPT sensor and tighten its retainer to the specified torque, reconnect the electrical connector, then refit the engine appearance cover and tighten its nuts to their specified torque.
edits.why: This restores the sensor mounting and electrical connection before the cover closes access. Keep each fastener specification with its own component.
